PR Summary by Qodo

Default omitted wicket confirmations for legacy mobile payloads 🐞 Bug fix 🧪 Tests 📝 Documentation 🕐 20-40 Minutes
AI Description

>
>• Defaults omitted dismissal confirmations based on wicket kind for legacy payload compatibility.
>• Aligns JSON schema and protocol invariants with optional confirmation fields.
>• Tests omission handling and normalizes confirmed non-dismissals to false.
>
Diagram

```mermaid graph TD Legacy["Legacy Payload"] -->|omits flag| Model["Wicket Model"] -->|defaults true| Scoring["Cricket Scoring"] -->|counts wicket| Snapshot["Score Snapshot"] --> Gateway["Live Gateway"] --> Mobile["Mobile Banner"] Snapshot --> Fantasy["Fantasy Points"] Snapshot --> Social["Social Post"] ```
High-Level Assessment

>The following are alternative approaches to this PR:
1. Default missing confirmations to false
- ➕ Preserves the documented functional truth that missing confirmation means not out. - ➕ Accepts legacy payloads without creating false wickets or downstream side effects. - ➖ Historically counted dismissals lacking the field would require later confirmation or correction.
2. Normalize in a version-aware boundary adapter
- ➕ Keeps the shared protocol strict and isolates legacy compatibility behavior. - ➕ Allows behavior to depend on known client version or payload provenance. - ➖ Requires reliable client-version metadata and coordinated gateway or ingestion changes. - ➖ Adds another compatibility component to maintain.
3. Introduce a versioned event contract
- ➕ Makes the semantic change explicit rather than silently changing existing payload meaning. - ➕ Supports a controlled migration and eventual removal of legacy behavior. - ➖ Requires producer and consumer coordination across repositories. - ➖ Has greater short-term delivery and operational cost.
>**Recommendation:** Do not use an unconditional true default when omission functionally means not out. Prefer a version-aware boundary adapter with false as the unknown-payload fallback; if provenance cannot be determined, retaining explicit validation is safer than propagating false wickets across scoring, fantasy, social, and mobile systems.

2. Malformed wicket data passes validation 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>_confirmed_only_with_dismissal now rewrites an explicit confirmed wicket whose kind is none to

>Code >

>
>Evidence >
> >
>The after-validator now returns a modified model for the contradictory combination, and the changed
>test explicitly verifies acceptance rather than the previous validation error.

Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >An explicitly confirmed wicket with no dismissal kind is malformed, but the new validator silently rewrites it and hides the producer error. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- cricket_protocol/models.py[52-56] >- tests/test_models.py[47-51] > >## Recommended Fix >Restore validation failure when `kind` is `none` and `umpire_confirmed` is explicitly true. Keep omission compatibility separate in the before-validator and restore a test asserting that contradictory explicit input raises `ValidationError`. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
3. Clients receive conflicting defaults 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>The JSON schema advertises an unconditional true default, while _default_omitted_confirmation
>assigns false when kind is none and the after-validator also normalizes explicit true to false.
>A schema consumer applying the published default therefore represents the same non-dismissal

No default. False means the dismissal does not count." >+ "default": true, >+ "description": "Optional. Defaults to true for older mobile clients that omit the field." >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The schema's new default has no condition on kind, whereas the runtime derives the omitted value
>from whether the kind equals none; the two contracts therefore disagree for a valid non-dismissal
>object.
